byuhati: Byūhati, [denom．fr．byūha] to stand in array (like a troop) VvA．104 (byūhanto, v．l．brahmanto) ． (Page 492)
byadhita: Byādhita, [pp．fr．byādheti] afflicted with disease Th．1, 73; Miln．168． (Page 492)
byabadha: Byābādha, [vy+ā+bādh] evil, wrong, hurt; usually referred to as 3 fold: atta°, para°, ubhaya°, or against oneself, against others, & both -- M．I, 416; S．IV, 159 (vyā°) , 339． (Page 492)
byapada: Byāpāda, [fr．vy+ā+pad] ill-will, malevolence, one of the 5 “obstructions＂ (āvaraṇāni, see e．g．S．V, 94; Nd2 379) ; and of the 4 “bonds＂ (kāya-ganthā see e．g．Nd1 98) ．-- M．I, 434; S．I, 99; It．119; Ps．I, 31; II, 12; Nd1 149, 207, 386． --vitakka a malevolent or angry thought M．I, 11; S．I, 203; II, 151; III, 93; V, 417; Nd1 501; Kvu 113． (Page 492)
byaga: Byagā, 3rd sg．aor．of vi+gam, to depart, to be lost, perish Th．1, 170．Byaggha [cp．Sk．vyāghra] a tiger J．II, 110; Sdhp．388．f．byagghinī Miln．67． (Page 492)
byapanna: Byāpanna, [fr．vyāpajjati] malevolent Sdhp．70; otherwise vy°, e．g．S．II, 168 (°citta) ． (Page 492)
byabadheti: Byābādheti, [denom．fr．byābādha] to injure, hurt, oppress S．V, 393 (na kiñci byābādhemi tasaṁ vā thāvaraṁ vā) ． (Page 492)
byanjana: Byañjana, (nt．) [cp．Sk．vyañjana] 1．sign, mark: see vyañjana．-- 2．the letter, as compared with attha, the spirit or meaning; thus in phrase atthato byañjanato ca according to the meaning & the letter Miln．18, 345; Nett 23．As vyañjana is the more usual (& classical) form, other refs．will be found under vyañjana． (Page 492)
byaruddha: Byāruddha, [pp．of vy+ā+rundh; reading by° in Nd1; vy° in Sn．& SnA; v．l．BB] obstructed, opposed, hindered Sn．936 (aññam-aññehi b．in enmity with each other; =paṭiviruddha Nd1 408) , 938 (412 id．; SnA 566=āhata-citta) ． (Page 492)
byattata: Byattatā, (f．) [fr．byatta] experience, learning Miln．349．See also pari°． (Page 492)
byabhangi: Byābhaṅgī, (f．) [vy+ā+bhañj] 1．a pole for carrying burdens Th．1, 623．-- 2．a flail S．IV, 201． (Page 492)
byama: Byāma, [cp．Vedic & P．vyāma cp．Śatap．Br．I．2, 5, 14 a fathom, measured by both hands being extended to their full length, only in phrase °ppabhā a halo extending for a fathom around the Buddha J．I, 12, 90; Bu I．45; Miln．75; VvA．213． (Page 492)
byadheti: Byādheti, [Caus．fr．byādhi] to cause to waver, unsettle, agitate, trouble S．I, 120; Th．1, 46, 1211．Pass．byādhiyati Kvu II．457 (aor．byādhiyiṁsu) ．-- pp．byādhita． (Page 492)
byuha: Byūha, [cp．Sk．& P．vyūha fr．vi+vah] 1．the array or arrangement of troops in particular positions, order of parade or battle DA．I, 85．Three formations of troops are mentioned at J．II, 404 & 406, viz．paduma-vyūha (lotus formation) , cakka° (wheel formn) , sakaṭa° (cart formn) ．-- 2．a heap, collection, in byūhaṁ karoti to put into a (well-arranged) heap Miln．2 (kacavaraṁ) ．‹-› 3．a (blind) alley, cul-de-sac Vin．IV, 271 (byūhan nāma yen’eva pavisanti ten’eva nikkhamanti) ． (Page 492)
byavata: Byāvaṭa, [vy+ā+vṛ] covered, adorned with VvA．213 (rūpakāya byāvaṭa jana; v．l．byāgata) ． the meaning (wrongly given as “adorned＂) is to be deleted．The reading at VvA．213 is doubtful．It may be kāyavyāvaṭa, but dassana-vyāvaṭa is to be preferred (see under vyāvaṭa) ． (Page 492)
byamha: Byamha, [cp．vyamha] a celestial mansion, a Vimāna Vv 523．As vyamha at J．IV, 464． (Page 492)
byasatta: Byāsatta, [pp．of vy+ā+sañj, cp．āsatta1] attached to, clinging to, in cpd．°mānasa possessed with longing Dh．47 (=sampatte vā asampatte vā lagga-mānasa DhA．I, 361) , 287 (cp．DhA．III, 433; lagganatāya sattamānasa) ． (Page 492)
bya: Byā, (indecl．) [distorted fr．iva=eva, with metathesis & diaeresis *veyya›*veyyā›*vyā›byā] intensive particle: “just so, certainly, indeed＂ only in phrase “evaṁ byā kho＂ Vin．II, 26; IV, 134=DA．I, 27; M．I, 130 (evaṁ vyā kho ti evaṁ viya kho C．) , 257． (Page 492)
byappatha: Byappatha, [so for byappattha; according to Kern, Toev．s．v．the word is a distortion fr．*vyāpṛta (for which usually P．vyāvaṭa) of vy+ā+pṛ3, pṛṇoti to be busy or active] busy, active．Thus Kern, but the trsln is not satisfactory．It occurs only at 2 passages; Vin．IV, 2, where combd with vācā, girā, vacībheda, and meaning “mode of speech, ＂ and at Sn．961, where it has the same meaning & is referred by Nd1 472 to a mode of speech & expld by SnA 572 by vacana．Thus the derivation fr．pṛ with vyā° can hardly be claimed to be correct for Bdhgh’s conception of the word; to him it sounded more likely like vy+ā+patha (cp．cpds．vacana-patha & vāda-patha) , thus “way of speaking．＂ (Page 492)
byadhi: Byādhi, [cp．Sk．vyādhi; lit．“upset＂ fr．vy+ā+dhā] sickness, disease A．I, 146; Kvu II．457; Miln．351． (Page 492)
